key_insight: Bayesian data assimilation can calibrate simple differentiable RANS turbulence closures and inlet conditions directly from noisy 3D flow MRI while preserving predictive mean-flow reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to improve CFD models for complex internal flows using experimental imaging data, with quantified uncertainty for design and validation.
method: Use noisy 3D flow MRI measurements from the FDA nozzle as observational data.
Infer posterior distributions for turbulence-model parameters and inlet boundary conditions in an inverse RANS formulation.
Compare two algebraic closures: one based on mean shear-rate magnitude and one based on turbulence kinetic energy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the inferred models reconstruct the measured mean velocity field without overfitting and provide uncertainty estimates for the fitted parameters.
watch_item: The approach depends on differentiable RANS closures, so extension to more complex or non-differentiable turbulence models may require additional formulation work.
paper_title: Data assimilation of flow MRI data into RANS models with algebraic closures
